choices: Running JavaScript outside the browser, including on a server
questions.explanation: Node.js took the V8 JavaScript engine out of Chrome and packaged it as a standalone runtime. This is what made server-side JavaScript possible — the same language you use to update a DOM element can now handle HTTP requests, read files, or query a database.

choices: It replaces the need for Node.js
It's a framework for building a web server with Node.js, including defining routes
questions.explanation: Express is a minimal web framework layered on top of Node.js. It handles the boilerplate of an HTTP server — parsing requests, routing URLs to handler functions, sending responses — so you don't have to implement all that from scratch.

questions.q: What is middleware in an Express app?
choices: A type of database used only for caching
A function that runs between receiving a request and sending a response
The HTML template rendered to the browser
A CSS preprocessor for styling routes
questions.explanation: Middleware functions sit between an incoming request and the outgoing response — parsing bodies, logging, checking authentication, and more. Each one calls next() to pass control along, or can short-circuit by sending a response early. Most of what happens in a real Express app happens in middleware before any route handler runs.
